rationale: Charter fidelity is substantially achieved: all six settled facts from mindspec-aytt are carried with re-derivation (fact 6 was re-verified against post-127 main exactly as the charter demanded, and the correction is honestly labeled); the deterministic #248 plan-approve warning is captured fixture-shaped (R3.1, AC-5) per the charter's AC; the two charter-mandated open questions (ADR-0041 §1 reversal, ADR-0023 C1-1) are posed as OQ-1/OQ-2 with the mandated framing (no 'APPLIED, no amendment' language; R1's on-disk-derivation proposal carried as an option); every WHAT-MOVES subcomponent of #220/#186/#179/#187/#146-remainder/#221 maps to a requirement, including the four #146 sub-items and #221's literal shipped adopt invocation; #179 is rebuilt on settled fact 2 rather than relitigated; and OQ-6 honestly records the lost ROUND3-CONSOLIDATION handoff instead of pretending the 9-question inventory is complete. #245/#248 are additive adjacencies, not scope drift (the charter's evidence section itself assigns the wrong-hint fixture to 128, and R3.4 draws an explicit fence against 127's destructive-hint class). However, three of the deliberately-posed questions are partially pre-decided by requirement wording, and the R6.3-vs-#255 deferral boundary has a seam that lets both specs disclaim the partial-filter-drop defect. These are wording/AC fixes, not design flaws, hence REQUEST_CHANGES without hard_block.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 (and the internal/panel entries in Impacted Domains and In Scope): condition the GateFacts-feeding language on OQ-1 resolving to (c). As written, 'Whichever mechanism: the fact is computed on the complete/caller side and fed into panel.GateFacts' mandates option-(c) machinery unconditionally — under (a) reorder or (b) rollback there is no staleness fact to compute or feed, so the clause is either unsatisfiable or forces (c). Reword to e.g. 'if the chosen mechanism involves a staleness-exemption fact, that fact is computed caller-side and fed into GateFacts…', and mark the internal/panel scope entries as conditional on OQ-1(c).

R6.3: promote the drop-loudness claim to a normative, AC-pinned requirement or explicitly assign it. R6.2 asserts 'R6.3 makes any drop loud rather than silent', but R6.3's only normative sentence covers the positional-bead-ID error case (pinned by AC-10); the no-positional list path — where the step-2.5 filter silently drops some-but-not-all bd-ready items, shifting --pick indexing (Background residue #2, confirmed at next.go:430-438) — has no requirement and no AC in this spec, and spec-129's #255 covers only the all-dropped 'no ready work' false-done outcome. As bounded today, both specs can disclaim the partial-drop defect. Either add a requirement (when the filter excludes any bd-ready item from the displayed set, the output names the excluded items/count and the reason) with an AC, or name the partial-drop disclosure explicitly in the Non-Goals #255 entry so exactly one spec owns it.

OQ-5 / R6.2 / AC-9: reconcile the ordering question with the requirements that already settle it. R6.2 sentence 1 mandates preserving bd-ready order end-to-end with no post-query reordering, and AC-9 hardcodes 'selection order equals the bd ready --parent returned order' — so OQ-5's 'plan order / lowest bead number' option is foreclosed as an ordering choice, and OQ-5's closing claim that 'AC-9's ordering assertion pins whichever choice is made' is false (AC-9 pins bd order regardless). Either narrow OQ-5 to what is genuinely open (the default-pick rule over a settled bd-ordered display, noting a non-first default clashes with the quoted 'Defaulting to first item' output), or genuinely parameterize R6.2/AC-9 on the OQ-5 resolution.

OQ-3 option 3: state the evidence bar for taking it, or strike it. The option is honestly flagged as relitigating settled fact 1, but the charter says 'do not relitigate' flatly; if the option is to remain listed, name the escape standard (audited refutation with evidence, per the established gate discipline) so the plan panel cannot take it as an ordinary design choice.

findings.title: OQ-1 quietly tilted to option (c) by R4.2's unconditional GateFacts clause
findings.detail: OQ-1 claims the spec 'deliberately does not choose' among (a) reorder / (b) rollback / (c) tracker-only staleness exemption, and R4.1/R4.4 genuinely hold under all three. But R4.2's second sentence — 'Whichever mechanism: the fact is computed on the complete/caller side and fed into panel.GateFacts' — is (c)'s machinery stated as an unconditional requirement: under (a) the gates run before the commits exist (no delta to exempt) and under (b) the tip is restored to reviewed_head_sha (no fact needed). Impacted Domains ('internal/panel/** (R4: consumes a caller-computed tracker-only fact only)') and In Scope ('internal/panel/gate.go (consuming a caller-computed fact only)') repeat the presupposition without a conditional. A plan reviewer reading the requirements as binding would conclude (c) is already mandated, which contradicts the charter's pose-do-not-assume framing that OQ-1 exists to honor.

findings.title: R6.3-vs-#255 boundary lets both specs disclaim the partial-filter-drop defect
findings.detail: The deferral boundary is honest for the two named faces: R6.3 owns the positional false-error (AC-10) and #255 owns the all-dropped false-'no ready work' spec-done outcome. But the middle case — filter drops some-but-not-all bd-ready items on the no-positional path, silently shifting --pick/display indexing versus bd ready's rows — is covered by neither: R6.3's normative text is positional-only (its lead-in 'may not silently change selection semantics' has no list-path AC), and #255's outcome class as described in Non-Goals is only the false-done terminal. R6.2 papers over this by citing 'R6.3 makes any drop loud rather than silent' — a requirement R6.3 does not actually contain. Verified at the tree: runEmitOnly filters by containsSpecID then takes items[0] with no disclosure (cmd/mindspec/next.go:430-445); the claim path filters identically at :178-186. This is precisely the both-specs-disclaim seam the split must not have, and it sits inside #187's chartered scope (the pick/row-disagreement face is described in Background residue #2 but never required away or disclosed-by-requirement).

findings.title: OQ-5 is pre-decided by R6.2 sentence 1 and AC-9, and OQ-5 misdescribes AC-9
findings.detail: OQ-5 poses 'bd-ready order vs plan/bead-number order' as open, deferring to plan time. But R6.2's first sentence requires the ready set to 'preserve bd ready's returned order end-to-end; no post-query step reorders it', and AC-9 asserts 'selection order equals the bd ready --parent returned order' unconditionally. Under those, resolving OQ-5 to plan/bead-number order is unimplementable as an ordering (reordering is forbidden and AC-9 would be red), and survives only as a default-pick-non-first-row rule — which contradicts R6.2's own quoted 'Defaulting to first item' output and muddies the pick-N-indexes-displayed-rows contract. OQ-5's closing claim that 'AC-9's ordering assertion pins whichever choice is made' is false as written: AC-9 pins bd order regardless of the choice. Genuinely open questions must not be constrained to one live answer by requirement wording.

findings.title: OQ-3 option 3 opens a relitigation path for settled fact 1 without naming the evidence bar
findings.detail: Listing the derive-implement-when-children-exist option with an explicit 'flagged: this relitigates settled fact 1' is more honest than omitting it, but the charter's instruction is 'do not relitigate' with no stated escape. The project's own gate discipline (any-RC-blocks with audited-refutation escape) supplies the right shape: if the option stays, the OQ should state that taking it requires an audited refutation of the settled fact's evidence (ADR-0023 table row + derive.go all-open branch + three independent 127-gate slots), not an ordinary plan-time preference.

findings.title: BRIEF: charter method mandate 'Keep both' only half-carried
findings.detail: The aytt charter's method note says every 127 defect was caught by (1) a mandatory 'errors in this brief' report item plus (2) reviewers explicitly licensed to contradict the orchestrator, and says 'Keep both.' This round's BRIEF carries the license ('you are explicitly licensed to contradict… report it as a finding') but not the mandatory report item — nothing in the verdict schema or reviewer instructions requires each slot to affirmatively report on BRIEF errors (including 'none found'). Reported per the BRIEF's own errors-in-this-BRIEF licensing; the fix belongs in the panel BRIEF template for subsequent rounds, not in spec.md.

findings.title: Charter fidelity positives (for the tally's record)
findings.detail: All six settled facts carried and re-derived (fact 6's stale {"mode":""} claim corrected exactly as the charter demanded); fixture-shaped #248 evidence delivered (R3.1/AC-5 capture the exact epic state alongside the 2026-07-25 warning text as golden baseline); charter-mandated OQ-1/OQ-2 posed with the required framing; all WHAT-MOVES subcomponents of the six issue clusters present (including #146's four sub-items as R6.2/R6.4/R6.5/R6.6 and #221's literal 'mindspec impl adopt <spec-id> --reason' naming); #179 rebuilt on settled fact 2; OQ-6 honestly discloses the lost 9-question handoff inventory rather than claiming completeness; the 127-vs-128 hint-class fence (destructive vs self-worsening) is drawn explicitly in R3.4.
